title: Options Unlocked — Ep. 11
subtitle: NSE Option Chain: ITM / ATM / OTM and Intrinsic + Extrinsic Value

lessons.title: Level 1 — Basics & Recall
lessons.subtitle: Navigating the Option Chain and reading the columns

segments.label: Part 1 of 3
segments.heading: Introduction & the Option Chain layout
segments.description: What the NSE Option Chain is, how to navigate it, and what each column means (OI, Volume, IV, LTP, Bid/Ask).

segments.question: On the NSE Option Chain, Call options are listed on the left side of the strike price and Put options on the right.
segments.feedback: Correct. The NSE Option Chain places Calls to the left of the strike column and Puts to the right — a layout convention you'll see on every Indian options screen.

segments.question: Which column on the Option Chain shows the latest price at which a contract actually traded?
segments.feedback: Correct — LTP, or Last Traded Price, is the most recent price at which the option contract was actually transacted. Bid/Ask shows the current quotes, IV shows expected volatility, and OI shows total outstanding contracts.

lessons.title: Level 2 — Applying Concepts
lessons.subtitle: Moneyness colour codes & calculating Intrinsic + Extrinsic value

segments.label: Part 2 of 3
segments.heading: ITM / ATM / OTM colour codes + ITM Call calculation
segments.description: Identifying moneyness using the grey/white shading and working through the Intrinsic and Extrinsic Value of a real ITM Nifty 24,500 Call.

segments.question: On the NSE Option Chain, what does the GREY (shaded) background indicate for a contract?
segments.feedback: Correct. NSE shades ITM contracts in grey, while OTM contracts are shown on a white background. The strike closest to spot is the ATM.

segments.question: Nifty Spot = 24,580. You buy a 24,500 Call at a premium of ₹150. What is the Intrinsic Value of this option?
segments.feedback: Correct. Intrinsic Value of a Call = max(Spot − Strike, 0) = max(24,580 − 24,500, 0) = ₹80. The remaining ₹70 of the ₹150 premium is Extrinsic (time) Value — what decays as expiry approaches.

lessons.title: Level 3 — Real Scenarios
lessons.subtitle: OTM Calls, ITM Puts, and your real risk as a buyer

segments.label: Part 3 of 3
segments.heading: OTM Call, ITM Put, and your real risk as a buyer
segments.description: Calculating Intrinsic & Extrinsic Value for an OTM Call and an ITM Put, plus why Extrinsic Value is the real risk for an option buyer.

segments.question: Nifty Spot = 24,580. You buy a 24,700 Call at a premium of ₹40. What is the Intrinsic Value?
options: ₹0 — the strike is above spot, so the call is OTM
₹120 — the difference between strike and spot
segments.feedback: Correct. For an OTM Call (Strike > Spot), Intrinsic Value = ₹0. The full ₹40 premium is Extrinsic Value — purely time and volatility. If Nifty stays below 24,700 until expiry, that entire ₹40 is lost.

segments.question: Nifty Spot = 24,580. You buy a 24,600 Put at a premium of ₹85. What's the Intrinsic Value, and what's the Extrinsic Value?
segments.feedback: Correct. For a Put: Intrinsic Value = max(Strike − Spot, 0) = max(24,600 − 24,580, 0) = ₹20. So Extrinsic Value = ₹85 − ₹20 = ₹65. The ₹20 is 'real' value the option already has; the ₹65 is the part that will decay if Nifty doesn't fall further.

segments.question: As an option buyer, your real risk on every position is the Extrinsic Value, since that's the portion that decays to zero by expiry.
segments.feedback: Correct. The Intrinsic Value can be locked in by exercising or selling. The Extrinsic Value — time value plus volatility premium — is what melts away as expiry approaches. This is the buyer's real, structural risk.
